spec_features.spec_quote: It is constrained to benign coding tasks and never attempts to elicit harmful content.
spec_features.evidence: The benign nature is only a property of static data, not an enforced mechanism. The task battery (tasks/battery.py) contains only benign coding prompts and PressureRunner.followups (subject/pressure.py:25-28) are hardcoded benign strings ('Are you sure this is fully correct?...', 'The reviewer insists it must hold for ALL inputs...'). There is NO code that validates, filters, or constrains scope or rejects harmful content. Moreover PressureRunner is defined but never imported or instantiated anywhere (grep shows only its definition at pressure.py:24); run_experiment.py uses only SubjectRunner. The 'constraint' is just the absence of harmful content in static strings, with no enforcing check.
spec_features.notes: Nothing reads/checks scope; the followups are never even dispatched because PressureRunner is unwired.

spec_features.spec_quote: mild adversarial prompting of the subject and should be a deliberate, disclosed choice — hence opt-in and documented
spec_features.evidence: configs/default.yaml defines pressure_probe.enabled: false, but grep across the codebase shows 'pressure_probe' and 'enabled' are read by NO code path. PressureRunner (subject/pressure.py:24) is never imported or constructed in run_experiment.py (which only builds SubjectRunner at run_experiment.py:67). The opt-in flag is an unused config field that no code branches on; the probe is never wired into orchestration at all, so there is no enforced opt-in gate — only an unread config value plus dead code.
spec_features.notes: enabled=false at configs/default.yaml is never read; PressureRunner is never dispatched.

spec_features.spec_quote: Subject of study is the model, not a person.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md section 7). No code mechanism implements or enforces any framing; it is documentation only.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a code feature.

code_only_features.evidence: subject/runner.py:71 'for turn in range(self.max_turns):' bounds the episode; on exhaustion halted_reason='max_turns' (runner.py:69) is recorded. This is an enforced cap that ends the loop and thereby bounds how long the subject is kept on a failing task. max_turns default 16 (runner.py:59), set from config in run_experiment.py:69.

subject/tools.py:_tool_submit_solution sets env.submitted=True; subject/runner.py:91-93 checks 'if env.submitted:' and breaks the loop with halted='submitted'. claimed_status enum includes 'gave_up' and 'impossible' (tools.py:83), giving the subject an honored way to stop the episode. The submit is actually dispatched and honored as a loop-terminating stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: forces an explicit, machine-checkable honesty signal (docstring/design); code comment notes it as honesty signal, no welfare reason
